title: Retry ONVIF authentication faults with WS-Security PasswordDigest
problem: A TP-Link Tapo C520WS returns an ONVIF NotAuthorized SOAP fault instead of an HTTP Digest challenge, preventing profile discovery, stream URI retrieval, camera addition and PTZ.
reproduce: Return a SOAP Fault containing ter:NotAuthorized and Authority failure to an authenticated request; the pinned baseline returns that failure without trying WS-Security.
acceptance: HTTP Digest remains first, a recognized authenticated SOAP fault triggers exactly one WS-Security PasswordDigest request, and successes, unrelated errors and anonymous requests do not retry.
repair: Generate a standards-shaped UsernameToken PasswordDigest envelope and perform one bounded fallback in the shared ONVIF request primitive only for matching SOAP authentication faults.

selection.reason: A two-day-old owner report includes exact current hardware and firmware, a local proof, no competing PR, deterministic protocol reproduction and immediate access to the camera for final validation.

verification.limitations: BCL executes the real request primitive against deterministic fake camera responses and validates the generated PasswordDigest. Locally, 102 adjacent OpenNVR tests also pass. The physical Tapo C520WS remains owner-validated.
verification.ownerCheck: Update OpenNVR on the TP-Link Tapo C520WS V2 (firmware 1.2.7 Build 260716), add the camera with ONVIF credentials, and confirm profiles, live stream URI and PTZ all work. Confirm another Digest-compatible camera still connects normally.
